cases.name: README example: decode
cases.note: The library returns {latitude, longitude} objects; the values are the same.

cases.name: negative half tie rounds toward +infinity
cases.note: Written for polytini from the README description (the package ships no tests): it quantizes with Math.floor(value * 10^precision + 0.5), so -0.5 becomes 0. polytini rounds half away from zero, as Google's algorithm does, so -0.5 becomes -1.

cases.name: overlong (noncanonical) value is rejected
cases.note: Written for polytini from the README description (the package ships no tests): a value whose last group is 0 after another group ("a?" is a two-group spelling of 1) throws "invalid". polytini follows the algorithm, which only defines how to read the groups, and accepts it.

cases.name: decoded latitude outside [-90, 90] is rejected
cases.note: Written for polytini from the README description (the package ships no tests): decoded points outside latitude [-90, 90] or longitude [-180, 180] throw. polytini does not check ranges: the format stores any number, and factor or order options change what the values mean.

cases.name: precision 8 is rejected
cases.note: Written for polytini from the README description (the package ships no tests): precision must be 0 to 7. polytini allows 0 to 15 and computes with exact integers up to 2^53.

cases.name: truncated pair throws
cases.note: Written for polytini from the README description (the package ships no tests): an incomplete lat/lon pair throws "truncated". polytini does the same.
